validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented proposed project. Tellurian Inc. launched a binding open season for the Delhi Connector Pipeline (DCPL) in April 2019 (oilandgas360.com, 2019-04-29, headline-level confirmation), and Tellurian's own site (Wayback capture 2021-05-07, content dated to 2020-08-13) describes 'Delhi Connector Pipeline LLC ("DCPL"), a subsidiary of Tellurian Inc., ... proposing to construct, own and operate, an ~180-mile long, 42-inch diameter interstate natural gas pipeline' originating at Perryville/Delhi (Richland Parish, LA) and terminating near Lake Charles/Gillis, LA. A Feb-2020 Tellurian SEC Form 424B5 prospectus supplement independently confirms the same ~180-mile/42-inch/Perryville-Delhi-to-Lake Charles description. AEGIS Hedging (independent trade-analysis site, Dec 2020) and a Houston Chronicle wire story (Apr 2019, also carried by 1012industryreport.com) both independently corroborate scope, route and a $1.4B cost. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other roster row -- it is one of four related-but-distinct Tellurian/Driftwood supply pipelines (Haynesville Global Access Pipeline = P0285, Permian Global Access Pipeline (dropped by Tellurian per a 2020-12-02 NGI article, naturalgasintel.com), and Driftwood Pipeline LLC's own Line 200/Line 300 = a separate FERC-certificated project, flagged as a cross_row_lead below). Confirmed the $1.4B SegmentCost is explicitly and unambiguously attributed to 'a separate...project named the Delhi Connector Pipeline' (distinct from HGAP's $1B) in the Chron/wire story, resolving a possible HGAP-cost-misattribution concern in favor of the sheet's recorded value. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct -- a 42-in/180-mi/2 Bcf/d hub-to-hub interstate natural gas pipeline is a transmission trunk line, not gathering/distribution. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Delhi Connector Pipeline LLC' (100%) is correct and independently confirmed (EIA workbook + Tellurian's own site + SEC filing). CAVEAT (attribution context, not a value change): Tellurian Inc. was acquired by Woodside Energy in 2024; DCPL is now an indirect Woodside subsidiary (or dormant/dissolved -- no filing found either way), but since the project itself is dead (see status_reviews) I am not proposing an Owner1 change to 'Woodside' -- the project-level LLC name is the more precise and still-accurate entity of record. CAVEAT (capacity concept, not a spec concern): Tellurian's own site states 7.5 Bcf/d receipt / 5.0 Bcf/d delivery HYDRAULIC DESIGN capacity for the full pipe, while the sheet's recorded 2,000 MMcf/d (2 Bcf/d) matches every trade-press figure (AEGIS, Chron/wire, EIA) for the CONTRACTED/OPEN-SEASON target capacity -- these are different technical concepts, not a contradiction; the sheet's 2 Bcf/d figure is correct as the project's actual target throughput. CAVEAT (one outlier source, not adopted): a 2020-12-02 NGI article (about the unrelated Permian Global Access Pipeline) contains one sentence describing Delhi Connector as moving gas 'from Gillis to the Driftwood terminal site' -- the reverse direction of every other source (Tellurian's own site, SEC filing, AEGIS, Chron/wire, EIA, oilandgas360, and the routes-repo geometry, which runs from the Delhi/Richland-Parish end toward the Lake Charles/Gillis end). Treated as a garbled/erroneous single sentence in an article about a different pipeline, outweighed 4:1 by independent, detailed, on-topic sources; not adopted. ROUTE: the routes-repo geometry for P2523 (one LineString, 24 points, running ~[-91.54,32.41] near Delhi, LA to ~[-93.03,30.35] in the broader Lake Charles/Gillis corridor) is consistent with the sourced start/end description and is not one of the batch's flagged route-mismatch cases; not a hard mismatch, just schematic/approximate at the Gillis end.

cross_row_leads.facts: AEGIS Hedging (Dec 2020): 'Haynesville Global Access Pipeline LLC (HGAP), a subsidiary of Tellurian Inc., is proposing to construct a pipeline with 160-miles of 42-inch diameter pipe. The pipeline will transport gas from the Haynesville to Gillis in south Louisiana. A Final investment decision delayed until 2021. Construction had been planned to begin in 2022, with an in-service date of mid-2023.' Also independently corroborated by the Chron/wire story (1012industryreport.com): 'Tellurian's $1 billion Haynesville Global Access Pipeline will connect natural gas pipelines and production facilities in DeSoto Parish to those in Calcasieu Parish...Once complete in 2023, the 42-inch natural gas and 160-mile pipeline will transport up to 2 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day.'

Oil & Gas 360 (2023-04-26): FERC issued a certificate on April 21, 2023 authorizing Driftwood Pipeline, LLC's Line 200 and Line 300, an approximately $1.4 billion natural gas transmission project in Beauregard and Calcasieu Parishes, Louisiana, with combined capacity up to 5.5 Bcf/d using Baker Hughes electric-powered Integrated Compressor Line (ICL) technology. This is a SEPARATE, later, FERC-certificated Driftwood Pipeline LLC project -- distinct from Delhi Connector (which never reached FID/certification) -- likely relevant to whichever roster PID(s) cover Driftwood's Line 200/Line 300.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Dormancy math: EIA's own snapshot shows this project deferred/'On Hold' since 2020-08-14, and the sheet's own ShelvedYear=2021 (matching AEGIS's Dec-2020 report that FID had been pushed to 2021) is now, as of this Sept-2026 sweep, more than 5 years in the past with zero subsequent news of any kind -- clearing the >=4-year shelved-with-no-progress -> cancelled dormancy threshold by a wide margin. Per the prompt's instruction to test every shelved row for revival before recommending cancellation (a re-scoped project under a new name is not dead), I specifically researched what became of Tellurian's actual Gulf Coast gas-supply solution: Tellurian Inc. was acquired by Woodside Energy in 2024, and Woodside took a Final Investment Decision on Louisiana LNG on 2025-04-29 (woodside.com ASX announcement). The gas-supply infrastructure underpinning that FID is Kinder Morgan Louisiana Pipeline's newly filed 'Texas Access Project' (naturalgasintel.com, 2026, KMI as operator, Woodside as 1 Bcf/d anchor shipper) -- an entirely different pipeline, owned/operated by a different company (Kinder Morgan, not Tellurian/DCPL), on a different route (Jefferson County, TX into Cameron Parish, LA) than Delhi Connector's Perryville/Delhi-to-Gillis corridor. This positively RULES OUT a revival of Delhi Connector under a new name or scope -- Woodside's actual gas-supply build-out went a completely different direction. Corroborating (not cited as a formal ref, since it states nothing positively): delhiconnector.com, live-checked 2026-09-10, now resolves to a domain-parking redirect page ('window.location.href="/lander"'), consistent with total project abandonment. No FERC docket, SEC filing (Tellurian's FY2021-2025 10-Ks were not separately checked for this specific row, but no news search of any kind surfaced Delhi Connector again after Dec 2020), or trade-press mention of Delhi Connector was found after the Dec-2020 AEGIS article. Recommending Status='cancelled' rather than merely reaffirming 'shelved', with ShelvedCancelledType='inferred' and no fabricated ref for the inference itself (per standing rule) -- the >=4y-dormant-with-a-since-confirmed-alternative-solution combination is stronger evidence than a bare silence-only 'stale' call, but it is still an inference (no source explicitly states 'Delhi Connector Pipeline is cancelled'), hence tier=medium rather than high.
